schema.champion_commit: The last CONTENT commit of the generation, by definition. Never the commit that wrote this file: a state file cannot name its own commit, because its bytes are part of the tree that commit hashes. Generation 7 walked into that fixed point and needed a second commit to repair the pointer; generation 8 defines it away. Guarded by tests/test_loop_state_g8.py.
schema.bookkeeping_commit: null at write time, always. Nothing may fill this during the commit that writes the file, because the value would be that commit's own hash. A later generation reading git history may fill it; the null is the record that this one did not.
schema.machinery_commit: The commit every measurement in this generation ran against. One tree, one commit: the run manifest records it with dirty=false.
schema.results_commit: The commit carrying the artefacts and the result documents. Equal to champion_commit when the generation ends with its results.

pointer_provisional: This file is written by the commit that carries the results, so at the moment of writing the results commit does not yet exist and cannot be named -- the fixed point section 8 of the ruling describes. The pointer therefore names the machinery commit here and is repointed at the results commit by the following bookkeeping commit, which is the shape generation 7 used and the ruling ratified. This key is absent once the pointer is final.

open_findings.note: Amended by generation 8: writing with newline='' is only half the rule. Reading a CRLF file in text mode also normalises, so a read-modify-write round trip rewrites the whole file even when the write is careful. Generation 8 did exactly that to 20 tracked files and tests/test_line_endings_g6.py caught it before the commit. Tools that rewrite tracked files must open with newline='' on BOTH ends.

Opened at generation 8. run_witness_falsifier.py re-derived chart G by hand instead of importing it, so the generation-6 falsifier was a copy of the study it falsified and could only have detected a solver-level error, never a chart-level one. The witness result survives - g8 re-ran both through one class and got identical counts - but the independence the falsifier was supposed to supply was never there. Both now call ChartG; what remains open is that no falsifier in this repository has been audited for the same defect.

ruling_premises_corrected: Section 4's model of CHART-01 as 'two reconstruction operators ... silently selected by which entry point was called' understates it: five call sites in src/, nine in tests/, three grid resolutions, and a third hand-written copy of chart G inside the falsifier.

Section 5's 'a bare integer rank appears only where a gap justifies it - which today means d=4 only' is one word too strong. Chart J at d=4 has no gap at the cutoff, so the licence is chart G d=4 and chart L d=4, and d=4 is a coincidence of those two charts.

Section 7's retro-application of PH-22 cannot be honoured as a quotation: the operator's original text is not in the tree. It is recorded as a reconstruction from its points of use, marked as such, and its pre-SW-20 guard's missing controls are recorded rather than retro-fitted.

Section 8's test, generalised to 'the champion never touches a loop-state file', is false of correct history: 922c2cc, generation 7's own champion, modified LOOP_STATE_v4.json. The exact invariant - champion is not the commit that wrote the file - is what is asserted.
highest_remaining_scientific_risk: Every identifiability number in this repository is measured at ONE operating point. Generation 8 showed the local spectrum moves by 97% when the bias range changes and by 219% when the junction moves, both far more than the 2.8% the chart change produces - but it did not vary the operating point itself. The whole matched-d table, in all three charts, sits at witness pair 0 member a or a projection of it. Nothing measured here establishes that the ordering (observation set > junction > dimension > interpolant) holds at a different device, and the one axis generation 8 did not perturb is the one every cell shares.
second_remaining_scientific_risk: The basin counts of SPEC-g8-5 are weaker than they look, and the document says so. A null control - the same criterion over the same number of ordinary prior draws that form no witness pair - returns almost the member count in chart L at d=16, because two draws from a log-uniform box spanning two decades in each of sixteen coordinates are nearly certain to differ by more than 0.3 decades somewhere. The chart-L count is therefore close to trivial and is not quoted as anything else; the informative object there is the witness graph. What survives is only the qualitative answer: the witness set is not two devices. The barrier check that would settle it properly covers a stated sample rather than every pair, and walking every witness pair is the obvious next measurement.
not_supported_and_not_to_be_written: any rank fraction compared across charts - now three charts, not two
any frequency or probability of degeneracy in any chart; the chart-J search is further apart still, because its prior is not the same kind of prior
any contraction number at the instrument's own 2% noise
any bare integer rank outside the licensed cells, which explicitly includes chart J at d=4; licensed today: G_d4, L_d4
any full-spectrum comparison involving chart J without stating junction_scale - the spectrum of a mixed-unit Jacobian is not units-free and moves by a factor of ten across defensible scalings
any statement that an identifiable rank is a property of the device; it is a property of the (device, observation set) pair
'the chart does not move the rank' unqualified - true within one interpolant family, false outside it
any ordering of the sensitivities (observation set > junction > dimension > interpolant) as a general claim; it is measured at one operating point
